title: Position Reference Systems, Redundancy and Failure Awareness
description: The TDPO learns to treat position reference not as a single trusted number but as a pool of independent, imperfect systems the DP weights against each other. This domain also builds the vocabulary and judgement behind equipment class, redundancy and worst-case failure — the concepts that turn 'the vessel held position' into 'the vessel held position because it was designed to survive this specific failure.'
source_reference: DP Operator's Handbook 3rd ed (Bray) Ch.1-2; IMO MSC.1/Circ.1580 (Jun 2017)
sources: DP Operator's Handbook, 3rd Edition (Bray, Daniels, Fiander, Foster; The Nautical Institute) — Chapters 1-2
IMCA-published introduction to DP systems and operations — position reference systems and equipment class sections
IMO MSC.1/Circ.1580 — Guidelines for vessels and units with dynamic positioning (DP) systems — definitions, equipment classes, DP control system requirements

tasks.title: Working Near a Fixed Structure
tasks.setup: Position the vessel at moderate range from a virtual platform structure, with DGPS enabled as one of the active PRS and the vessel positioned downwind of the structure.
tasks.execute: Close on the structure per the exercise plan while watching DGPS position quality/scatter. Note any degradation as range decreases, and compare your wind sensor reading against the wind you'd expect given the logged environment.
professional_standard: Detected DGPS degradation from the data, not just from an alarm
Recognised the wind sensor reading as suspect before it caused a visible position problem
Could state which PRS types would NOT be expected to degrade in this scenario
Maintained a direct visual reference to the structure throughout, not just instrument watch

fields.label: Wind sensor reading vs expected true wind

debrief_questions: Why does a large fixed structure nearby specifically degrade DGPS, while an acoustic or laser-based PRS might be unaffected by the same proximity?

Working close-in on the downwind side of a platform, your wind sensor may be actively wind-shadowed rather than simply unreliable. What's the practical difference between those two failure types for a DPO trying to trust the reading?
What visual cues should tell you a positioning problem is developing near a structure before any instrument alarm fires?
If your only degraded PRS near the structure is DGPS, and you still have two other independent references online, should that change how concerned you are? Why or why not?

tasks.title: Equipment Class and Worst-Case Failure Identification
tasks.setup: Using the vessel's own FMEA or class documentation where available (or the exercise's provided vessel specification), identify the assigned equipment class and the worst-case failure it's designed to survive without losing position.
tasks.execute: With the vessel settled on DP, talk through what would actually happen to position-keeping if that specific worst-case failure occurred right now. Use the consequence analysis display if the system is fitted with one.
professional_standard: Correctly stated the vessel's equipment class from documentation, not assumption
Could describe the worst-case failure in specific terms (which thruster group, which bus section), not just 'a failure'
Correctly interpreted whether consequence analysis was currently showing margin or risk
Distinguished single-fault criteria from a total, unrealistic failure of everything at once
debrief_questions: In your own words: what actually separates equipment class 1, 2 and 3, in terms of the kind of failure the vessel must survive without losing position?

Consequence analysis continuously checks that the vessel could survive its worst-case failure right now, under present conditions. What's the practical difference in a real emergency between a vessel that has this running and one that doesn't?

A single inadvertent act by someone on board counts as a single fault under class 2/3 criteria. Can you think of a plausible inadvertent act on this vessel that could, on its own, cause the worst-case failure?
If the consequence analysis showed marginal capability on your present heading, what are your options, and which would you reach for first?

variants.title: Worst-Case Failure Under Degraded Power
variants.note_to_tdpo: Repeat with one generator already offline before you start. Notice how much the margin in the consequence analysis has already been eaten into before any new failure occurs.
